## 641f580d5310

**Reproduced semantic defect: the ordinary distribution excludes a canonical
self-mirror case and leaves a harmful shortcut alive.** Every canonical input is
odd-width and contains blue (`1`) cells on the vertical center axis: 3, 4, 5,
and 4 such cells across the three train pairs and test input. The generator's
invariant and `self_check`, however, require every `1` to satisfy `c < w // 2`.
Consequently all four canonical inputs are rejected; they also exceed the
implemented 3..7 count cap in three cases.

I tested 768 ordinary generated inputs (256 seeds in each band). None contained
a center-axis `1`. A wrong rival that copies the input and writes yellow (`4`)
at every blue cell's mirror coordinate—even when that coordinate is the source
itself—agreed with the correct background-conditional mirror repair on all 768
generated inputs. It disagreed on all four canonical inputs by overwriting their
self-mirroring blue cells. This is a concrete training-data shortcut, not merely
a style mismatch.

The same probe also found declaration/implementation drift: `AXES` advertises
`grid_h=4..12`, `grid_w=5..14`, and `n_ones=2..15`, while exact requests 12, 14,
and 15 are rejected by the narrower draw ranges. `palette_kind`, `palette_size`,
and `n_distinct_colors` overrides are silently accepted without changing the
realized one-color grid, and an undeclared `bogus=1` override is also silently
accepted.

Evidence: `checks/audit-probes.json` and `checks/audit-probes.log`. Suggested
repair: include ordinary odd-width center-axis witnesses, allow canonical one
counts, add the overwrite-at-self rival to the lesson gate, and either implement
or remove the nonfunctional axes while rejecting unknown keys.
